ai_summary.label: Why it matters
ai_summary.text: The massive non-cash charges significantly escalated the company's losses from $20 million a year earlier, despite an 89% increase in quarterly revenue to nearly $2 million.

ai_summary.label: What watch

aHR0cHM6Ly9kZWNyeXB0LmNvLz9wPTM3NTM1OQ==.rewritten_content:
Trump Media & Technology Group reported a net loss of $238 million for the second quarter, marking a substantial increase from the $20 million loss recorded during the same period a year earlier.

Financial Breakdown and Non-Cash Charges

The vast bulk of Trump Media's second-quarter loss stemmed from non-cash charges. These included over $190 million in unrealized losses spanning digital assets, pledged digital assets, and equity securities. According to a June SEC filing, the company recorded roughly $361 million in digital asset-related losses during the six months ended June 30. Despite these declines, Trump Media's quarterly revenue rose 89% to nearly $2 million, while total assets stood at $2 billion.

Crypto Holdings and Treasury Strategy Shifts

Trump Media's crypto holdings fell by more than 33% to $598 million by June 30, a total consisting of $558 million in Bitcoin and $41 million in Cronos. Concurrently, the firm abandoned plans for a Crypto.com-backed CRO treasury company and formally ended a broader digital asset agreement with the exchange.

As of June 30, the company held 9,477.16 Bitcoin, down slightly from 9,542.16 BTC at the end of the previous quarter. Of those holdings, 2,077.34 BTC were pledged as collateral for an options strategy, while 4,260.73 BTC served as collateral for convertible notes.

July Transactions and Final July 31 Valuation

In July, Trump Media sold Bitcoin-related securities worth $159.6 million and utilized the proceeds to purchase additional Bitcoin. By July 31, the company reported holding approximately 14,139 BTC, which included pledged Bitcoin, valued at about $890.5 million at the time.

Donald Trump remains the sole beneficiary of a trust that held approximately 41.1% of Trump Media's voting power as of Feb. 25. The company's ongoing financial reporting will track the net valuation impact of these expanded Bitcoin positions relative to its convertible note and options collateral obligations.

ai_summary.label: What happened
ai_summary.text: The Bank of Russia published a draft directive on August 11 outlining new rules for non-qualified investors to purchase cryptocurrencies through approved intermediaries.

ai_summary.label: Why it matters
ai_summary.text: The framework restricts public exchange trading to Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Tether's USDT, while imposing an annual purchase cap of 300,000 rubles per intermediary.

ai_summary.label: What to watch
ai_summary.text: The Bank of Russia is accepting public comments on the draft directive until August 24 before final sign-off by Governor Elvira Nabiullina.

aHR0cHM6Ly9kZWNyeXB0LmNvLz9wPTM3NTM0NQ==.rewritten_content:
The Bank of Russia has published a draft directive that establishes a formal pathway for non-qualified investors to purchase cryptocurrencies through registered brokers, crypto exchanges, or managers.

Asset Restrictions and Selection Criteria

Under the proposed regulatory framework, public exchange trading will be restricted to a select group of digital assets. Only Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Tether's USDT have been approved for the public exchange trading list, leaving prominent tokens such as XRP off the permitted asset roster.

To qualify for public exchange inclusion under federal law, digital assets must meet specific criteria. These requirements include evaluations of market capitalization, average daily trading volume, and a minimum of five years of pricing history recorded on foreign platforms.

Investment Caps and Mandatory Investor Testing

Non-qualified investors will face strict financial caps under the directive. The regulation sets an annual purchase limit of 300,000 rubles per intermediary. In contrast, qualified investors face no investment limits and maintain the legal ability to acquire all cryptocurrencies traded across both exchange and over-the-counter markets.

Regardless of investor classification, all participants must complete a mandatory testing process. This requirement obligates individuals to familiarize themselves with the inherent risks associated with cryptoassets before executing any trades.

Timeline and Implementation Steps

The regulatory text is subject to change based on public feedback. The Bank of Russia has opened a public comment period for the draft directive that remains active until August 24.

Once the feedback window closes, the directive requires an official signature from Bank of Russia Governor Elvira Nabiullina. The regulation is scheduled to take formal legal effect exactly 10 days after its official publication.

ai_summary.label: What happened
ai_summary.text: Luke Dashjr was removed as a Bitcoin Improvement Proposal editor through Pull Request 2248 in the bitcoin/bips repository.

ai_summary.label: Why it matters
ai_summary.text: The removal follows a motion citing editorial authority issues regarding BIP-110, a proposal to bar non-financial data like Ordinals inscriptions.

ai_summary.label: What to watch
ai_summary.text: Further governance updates within the bitcoin/bips repository following the addition of new editors in April 2024.

aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubmV3c2J0Yy5jb20vP3A9OTEy.rewritten_content:
Luke Dashjr has been removed from his position as a Bitcoin Improvement Proposal (BIP) editor following a controversy surrounding the BIP-110 proposal.

Pull Request 2248 and the Removal Motion

The administrative change removing Luke Dashjr was merged via Pull Request 2248 within the official bitcoin/bips repository. This update explicitly removed his name from the designated editor list in BIP 3. Fellow BIP editor Mark 'Murch' Erhardt initiated the removal by filing the motion on August 9.

Erhardt outlined four primary grounds for the removal action. These included exercising editorial authority inconsistent with established processes in a manner that favored Dashjr's own proposal, maintaining a minimal contribution level to the role, overseeing a soft fork proposal that evolved into a hard fork, and an overall breakdown in trust and coordination among contributors.

The BIP-110 Controversy and Metrics

The core of the dispute centered on BIP-110, titled a Reduced Data Temporary Softfork. The proposal sought to temporarily bar non-financial data, such as Ordinals inscriptions, from Bitcoin transactions. During its deployment window, support for BIP-110 peaked at 51 out of 2,016 blocks, representing approximately 2.53% of a total difficulty adjustment period.

Concurrent Departures

In addition to his removal from the BIP editor role, Luke Dashjr announced he was taking a sabbatical from his position as Chairman and CTO of mining pool Ocean. These governance and leadership changes occur alongside broader administrative updates to the BIP repository, which included the addition of supplemental editors in April 2024.

ai_summary.label: What happened
ai_summary.text: Bakkt published its Q2 2026 financial results on August 10, 2026, reporting $80.8 million of net income attributable to the company, driven largely by non-cash warrant revaluations.

ai_summary.label: Why it matters
ai_summary.text: The profitable quarter reverses a $14.7 million loss from a year earlier, though core revenue declined 70% to $170.1 million due to client transitions and softer digital-asset trading volumes.

ai_summary.label: What to watch
ai_summary.text: Whether Bakkt fully exercises its 47.5 million Transchem warrants within the 18-month window, which would require an additional payment of about $28.2 million.

aHR0cHM6Ly9jcnlwdG9zbGF0ZS5jb20vP3A9NTUz.rewritten_content:
Bakkt posted $80.8 million of net income attributable to the company in its Q2 2026 financial results, published on August 10, 2026.

Earnings Reversal Driven by Transchem Warrants

The net income figure of $80.8 million completely reversed a $14.7 million loss recorded during the same period a year earlier. The primary driver behind the profit was a $98.5 million non-cash gain stemming from the revaluation of warrants in Transchem, an Indian listed company. A separate legacy warrant liability added another $1.4 million non-cash gain to the quarterly results.

According to a June 4 SEC filing, Bakkt paid $9.4 million—representing 25% of the subscription price—for 47.5 million Transchem warrants following their allotment in June. By June 30, 2026, this warrant position was carried on the company's balance sheet at $107.9 million. If Bakkt chooses to fully exercise these warrants within the 18-month timeframe, it would owe approximately $28.2 million more.

Revenue Contraction and Operating Expenses

In contrast to the warrant-driven net income gains, Bakkt's core operations experienced a significant contraction. Total revenue fell 70% to $170.1 million in Q2 2026, down from $568.1 million in the comparative prior-year period. The company attributed this steep revenue decline to client transitions and softer digital-asset trading volumes.

Crypto costs, execution, clearing, and brokerage fees totaled $169.3 million for the quarter. This left a calculated residual of about $0.9 million before accounting for other operating expenses. Consequently, Bakkt's operating loss from continuing operations widened to $19.6 million, compared to an operating loss of $16.1 million in the prior-year period. Adjusted EBITDA also reflected a deeper deficit, showing an $11.8 million loss compared with a $9.8 million loss a year earlier.

Cash Position and Financing Activities

Bakkt closed out the month of June 2026 with $50.7 million in cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash, while maintaining no long-term debt. During the first half of 2026, operational activities used $26.9 million of cash. Conversely, financing activities supplied $67.2 million over the same six-month period, driven primarily by equity offerings.
